source_snapshot.procedure: Manually choose a random date/time in the BMC WebUI, save it and check the resulting date/time; generic setup says clear logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: The date/time changes successfully and the displayed value matches the setting.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL retains manual WebUI plus IPMI verification but accepts random time, exposes credentials, assumes nonstandard `mc time get`, omits the remote target on a later read and does not define clock ownership, timezone, tolerance, NTP overwrite or restoration.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly replaces random time with a controlled value and requires WebUI/audit evidence, normalized multi-surface readback, time-sync policy and preserved event boundaries.

old_problem: A random time can damage audit chronology and time-dependent functions, while a green WebUI save state does not prove which clock changed or whether synchronization immediately replaced it. The proposed IPMI verification also relies on an unvalidated command and could read a different target or the SEL clock rather than the UI-managed clock.
disposition_reason: The source purpose is a real WebUI date/time mutation and visual confirmation. Replace unsafe randomness with one controlled Project-approved timestamp, retain before/save/after UI captures and use only vendor-documented API/IPMI surfaces as corroboration. The exact UI-managed clock, timezone, tolerance and NTP behavior are version-specific execution bindings; they do not prevent a complete Review-layer case. The prior IPMI SEL-clock row remains independent and cannot substitute for this WebUI path.
decision_basis: XLSX row 918, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, selection manifest, adjacent IPMI/DST rows and preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed.

The source explicitly requires manual WebUI setting, so screenshots or equivalent visual capture of target, entered value, save result and settled display are mandatory; API readback alone loses coverage.

The standard IPMI SEL clock is not automatically the OEM WebUI clock. Only version-specific vendor documentation may bind those surfaces; otherwise comparisons are recorded without inventing equivalence.

A controlled timestamp, approved tolerance, synchronization policy and reversible restoration convert the unsafe random operation into an auditable parameterized test without reducing the mutation requirement.

test_case.test_name: Set and verify BMC date/time through the WebUI under controlled synchronization policy
test_case.purpose: Verify the actual BMC WebUI Date and Time control accepts and visibly saves one controlled approved timestamp, displays the correct timezone-normalized value through the approved settling interval, produces an audit event and follows the documented relationship to vendor-supported API/IPMI/SEL surfaces and NTP policy.
required_package: Exact BMC asset/firmware/WebUI identity, authorized operator account and vendor documentation for the WebUI-managed clock
Owner-approved timestamp, trusted reference, timezone/DST context, numeric tolerance and immediate/settled observation interval
Current WebUI clock/timezone/NTP source and supported vendor API/IPMI/SEL comparison surfaces; no assumed `mc time get`
Impact check for certificates, tokens, schedules, power automation, audit consumers and concurrent time synchronization
Visual WebUI capture plus preserved BMC/SEL/audit evidence before, during and after the save
Approved restoration value and NTP/timezone policy with recovery access
test_case.test_command: STATE-CHANGING MANUAL WEBUI TEST; DO NOT EXECUTE WITHOUT APPROVAL. Preserve event/audit history and capture the verified target's Date and Time page, current value, timezone and synchronization source. Compare supported clock surfaces to a trusted reference and establish the vendor clock relationship. Use one explicit owner-approved timestamp—not random time—and obtain point-of-action approval. Manually enter and save it once in the WebUI while capturing the entered value, confirmation and audit event. Re-open/read the WebUI immediately and after the approved settling interval; compare only documented API/IPMI/SEL surfaces with timezone normalization and observe NTP behavior. Record the first post-change event, then restore or retain the approved policy. Never clear logs, guess commands, disable NTP or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: The verified WebUI visibly accepts the exact controlled value, the saved page and audit event identify that value, and immediate/settled displays are within the approved normalized tolerance or change exactly as documented by the active synchronization policy. Vendor-documented related clock surfaces agree as specified; unrelated SEL/host clocks are recorded but not falsely required to match. Logs remain preserved and the approved time/timezone/NTP policy is restored or retained.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires actual before/save/after WebUI visual evidence, exact requested timestamp, approved timezone/tolerance, settled display behavior, audit boundary and documented synchronization/cross-surface result. A save toast, API/IPMI output alone, random time or an assumed SEL-clock match cannot pass. Wrong clock/value/timezone, out-of-tolerance settled result, unexpected NTP overwrite, missing audit evidence or failed restoration is FAIL. Missing vendor semantics, tolerance, timestamp, approval or recovery is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS.
safety_gate: Do not clear SEL/audit/OS logs; preserve the pre-change boundary and first post-change evidence.
Verify target and exact WebUI page; do not substitute an API/IPMI write for the source's manual WebUI control.
Do not use random/local time, guess `mc time` support, assume SEL equivalence, disable NTP or alter timezone without explicit scope.
Assess certificate/schedule/token impact and obtain point-of-action approval before the one save.
Stop on ambiguous clock ownership, UI/API mismatch, sync overwrite or unexpected impact; do not click save again automatically.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/WebUI identity, approved timestamp/reference/timezone/tolerance/NTP policy and time-sensitive impact authorization
Visual before-state WebUI page plus supported vendor API/IPMI/SEL/reference reads and preserved audit/event boundary
Visual entered value, save confirmation and BMC audit event with exact target and timestamp
Immediate and settled WebUI display with normalized drift and documented NTP behavior
Vendor-documented cross-surface comparison, first post-change event chronology and explicit non-equivalence where applicable
Restored/retained approved policy, preserved logs, no-retry proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If the wrong clock/value/timezone is saved or time-sync behavior is unexpected, stop and preserve the WebUI/audit/SEL boundary. Through the verified WebUI/vendor method, restore the approved prior time/timezone/NTP policy only after fresh authorization, then re-read the UI and every documented related clock. Do not clear or rewrite logs and do not use repeated saves as trial-and-error recovery.

source_conflict.reason: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require the WebUI time control and displayed result. Randomness and missing clock-policy details are unsafe readiness gaps, not competing source purposes.

blocked.reason: The WebUI action, visual evidence, acceptance and recovery are defined. Firmware-specific clock mapping and time policy can be supplied as Project execution configuration.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: WebUI-managed clock semantics, controlled timestamp, reference/tolerance, timezone/NTP policy, supported comparison surfaces, impact approval and restoration plan.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; TIME/AUDIT STATE-CHANGING MANUAL WEBUI TEST; APPROVAL REQUIRED; NO CLOCK WRITE EXECUTED

project_authority: BMC vendor WebUI clock documentation, Project timezone/tolerance/NTP policy, time-sensitive impact rules and recovery SOP define execution acceptance.
